newsitem.title: FRANCE: Row with far-right annuls Paris region budget.
newsitem.headline: Row with far-right annuls Paris region budget.

text.p: The French government will directly administer the finances of the Paris region after the hung local council failed to pass its budget in a dispute with the far-right National Front, political sources said on Saturday.
The centre-right alliance which rules the Ile-de-France region, France's wealthiest, voted against its own budget plans on Friday night rather than accept the support of the Front.
Faced with opposition from the Left and Greens, the alliance of Gaullists and centrists would have needed the Front's support to push the budget through.
Under French law, regions unable to agree on their budget come under the direct control of the local prefect (government representative).
National Front regional leader Jean-Yves Le Gallou said the deadlock in the council showed the National Front "has become indispensible in Ile-de-France as well as in France as a whole".
Mainstream politicians are increasingly concerned by the rise of the Front, led by Jean-Marie Le Pen who won 15 percent of the vote in the 1995 presidential election.
The Ile-de-France row erupted as all-out battle loomed between the Gaullist RPR party of Prime Minister Alain Juppe and the National Front ahead of a general election due early next year.
The leadership Gaullist RPR party of Prime Minister Alain Juppe decided earlier this week to systematically oppose the Front which has vowed to prevent the Gaullists from retaining power.

The Front, which won control of three southern towns in 1995 local elections, campaigns for immigrants to be sent home. It wants French people to be given priority over foreigners for jobs and for French goods to be favoured over imported products.
